sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Senate Democrats Spend $5 Million in Kansas Ahead of Election
cards.content: Top Democrats are now investing in Kansas a state that hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate in nearly a century. This marks a shift in their strategy as they initially focused on core battleground seats. With just 22 days to go Senate Democrats are spending $5 million in Kansas where the gap is closing between Democrat Adam Hamilton and incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall. The move is part of a broader effort to flip seats in traditionally Republican areas including Texas Alaska and Iowa.

cards.title: Ebola patient travelled widely before diagnosis and death
cards.content: A Kenyan businessman traveled to several countries while sick with Ebola. He visited the Democratic Republic of Congo then Uganda and eventually Kenya where he was diagnosed and died two days later. The case highlights the limitations of relying on temperature checks and self-declarations to detect Ebola as the man's symptoms were initially misdiagnosed as a skin infection.

cards.title: Ukrainian Officer Claims Military Intelligence Authorized Monaco Bomb Attack
cards.content: A former Ukrainian security officer Vitalii Zhykovych says he believed a bomb attack in Monaco that hurt a businessman and his family was authorized by senior members of Ukraine's military intelligence agency. The businessman Vadym Yermolayev and his family were badly hurt in the blast. Zhykovych claims he was a freelancer for Ukraine's SBU security service and had nothing to do with the attack. He says Anastasia Berezovska the woman who planted the bomb was his agent and that she was not fully trained. Zhykovych also claims that another HUR officer Vladyslav Reut was involved and that Reut had proposed the operation.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Korea Developing Origami-Inspired Rover for 2030 Moon Mission
cards.content: Researchers at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science & Technology are developing a rover with innovative origami-inspired wheels to join South Korea's planned moon mission by 2030. The wheels are made of flexible strips that interweave mimicking the structure of a Da Vinci bridge and can shrink to fit inside a lunar lander and expand to explore the moon's surface. This technology could help the rover navigate the moon's challenging terrain and extreme temperature swings and it's hoped that a rover with these wheels will explore the moon's lava tubes which could one day shelter human colonies.

cards.title: University gets £3.67 million for Yorkshire robotics hub to boost industry
cards.content: A university in West Yorkshire has received £3.67 million to help companies use robotics technology. The Yorkshire Robotics Hub will help over 300 manufacturers adopt robotics and automation aiming to bridge the "automation gap". The project will create new jobs as more businesses use robots to increase efficiency. The UK currently has fewer robots per manufacturing employee than the global average so this hub will help the country catch up. The project will benefit the university by allowing it to work with local companies and improve research.

cards.title: Scientists Solve 180-Year-Old Mystery of Sun's Impact on Early Electrical Technology
cards.content: Scientists have solved a 180-year-old mystery about how the sun's weather affected early electrical technology. They found that a train that left Exeter 16 minutes late in the mid-1800s actually happened in 1848 not 1841 as previously thought. This changes our understanding of when the sun's weather first affected human technology. The researchers used a combination of historical records newspapers and scientific observations to figure out what happened. They found that the train delay was likely caused by a solar storm disrupting the electrical system which was a major problem for the telegraph networks of the time.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Nigerian Doctor Elected to Tackle Global Cancer Disparities
cards.content: Dr. Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu a Nigerian paediatrician has been elected president of the Union for International Cancer Control. She's the first African to hold the role and will focus on bridging the gap in cancer care between rich and poor countries. Cancer cases and deaths are expected to rise sharply especially in poorer countries and Bagudu wants to reorient global cancer policy to address this issue. She plans to use her position to bring attention to the need for better cancer care and to mobilize resources to strengthen prevention diagnosis and treatment.

cards.title: Temperature Key to Natural Sleep Cycles, Study Suggests
cards.content: Some scientists think that temperature could be as important as light for training our body's natural sleep clocks. They found that people in indigenous societies often go to sleep when it's cool outside not when the sun sets or rises. This suggests that temperature might be a cue for sleep just like light. Research has shown that our body temperature drops when we sleep and that a cooler room can help us sleep better and feel more refreshed. Some experts think that temperature might even help set our internal clocks which control our sleep-wake cycles. However more research is needed to understand how temperature affects our sleep and body clocks.

cards.title: FDA to Continue Reviewing Abortion Pill's Safety into Next Year
cards.content: The US Food and Drug Administration says it will continue reviewing the safety of a popular abortion pill into next year. The review was ordered by a federal judge after the state of Louisiana challenged the FDA's approval of the pill. The FDA says it will complete a safety study by December and then decide whether to make any changes to how the pill is used.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: El Niño Event Expected to Reach Record Strength in December 2026
cards.content: The ongoing El Niño event is expected to become the strongest on record since 1950 with a peak forecast around December 2026. Sea surface temperatures in the Pacific have already reached record levels with an anomaly of 3.7°C above normal expected. This means that around 2.6 billion people worldwide will experience unusually high temperatures through December.

cards.title: Wayanad's Temperature Soars 1.9°C Above Average, Hitting 34.4°C
cards.content: Wayanad a hill district in Kerala India is warming up more than usual. The Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology has been tracking the weather there for years and the data shows that the average temperature is now 1.9°C above what it used to be. The highest temperature recorded was 34.4°C which is unusually hot. The area is known for its cool and rainy climate which has shaped the local agriculture forests and tourism. The warming trend is worrying because it could have big consequences for the environment and the people who live there.

cards.title: UN Carbon Market Body Suspend Cookstove Project Credits
cards.content: At least 130 civil society organizations are calling on the United Nations carbon market body to suspend credits linked to a cookstove project in Myanmar. The project which became the first to receive carbon credits under the Paris Agreement's new carbon market mechanism in February 2026 has raised concerns about the reliability of emissions reductions independent verification and human rights safeguards. The groups are questioning whether the project's environmental integrity can be verified citing concerns over monitoring and verification processes and are demanding an independent investigation.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Ashmolean Museum Exhibition Explores Aphrodite's Evolution into Cultural Controversy
cards.content: Aphrodite the ancient Greek goddess of love and beauty has been a source of controversy for centuries. Her nudity has been a topic of debate and her artwork has been seen as objectifying the female body. A new exhibition at Oxford's Ashmolean Museum explores the history of Aphrodite showing how she evolved into a lightning rod of cultural controversy. The goddess has two versions of her origin story a mythological one and a historically accurate one and neither particularly marks her out as a troublemaker. She was initially a goddess of fertility love and procreation but later became associated with romantic love. The exhibition also looks at how Praxiteles's sculpture of Aphrodite the Aphrodite of Knidos changed everything by showing a fully nude female figure for the first time. This artwork was revolutionary and would go on to influence art for centuries to come.

cards.title: EbonyLife Place Opens in South-West London, Celebrating African Diaspora Stories
cards.content: A new cultural centre EbonyLife Place has opened in south-west London. It's a cinema and hub that showcases black and African movies music and art. The centre was founded by Nigerian media mogul Mo Abudu who wants to celebrate and share stories from the African diaspora. It has a cinema a bar a restaurant and a boutique and will host events like masterclasses and live performances.

cards.title: The Music Man Project Honors Sir David Amess with Standing Ovation in NYC's Town Hall
cards.content: A music group for people with learning disabilities The Music Man Project recently performed in New York's Town Hall a historic venue as a tribute to the late MP Sir David Amess. The group which was founded by Amess performed in front of a full house of almost 1500 people receiving a standing ovation. This performance was a fulfillment of Amess' dream before he was murdered in 2021. The group's founder David Stanley said the performance was a testament to what people with learning disabilities can achieve with support and high expectations.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Trump Announces Deal with Putin to Release 300000 Tonnes of Diesel Fuel
cards.content: US President Donald Trump has announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release Russian diesel fuel to the US and global markets. This move aims to lower diesel prices in America which have more than doubled since the US-Israel conflict with Iran began in February. The conflict has restricted global oil supplies leading to higher fuel prices. Trump's announcement includes the immediate supply of 300000 tonnes of diesel with more to follow. He says this will help farmers truckers and other Americans affected by high fuel costs.

cards.title: Boots sold to Canadian family's Wittington Investments
cards.content: Boots a well-known pharmacy and retailer in the UK has been sold to a new owner Wittington Investments a Canadian family that also owns Primark. This deal could change the way Boots operates its 1800 stores. Some experts think the new owners should invest in updating smaller stores which have lacked investment in the past. Others suggest Boots should make its stores more functional with health hubs not stuck in the corner. The company's loyalty card Advantage is popular and unlikely to change. Boots also plans to expand its healthcare services which could be a big part of its business in the future.

cards.title: Asos Warns of Data Breach Including Profiles and Search Histories
cards.content: Asos told its customers that hackers have detailed profiles of potentially millions of users including names addresses phone numbers emails and dates of birth. The hackers also have access to customers' search histories on the website. The company says no bank details or passwords were stolen but customers are warned about potential impersonation scams. The hackers gained access to the data by stealing an Asos employee's login credentials and using them to download the customer data.
